patient.activity: Independent and active; values walking, travel, and continued professional engagement

history.chiefConcern: Progressive bilateral leg pain with walking, right greater than left. Leg symptoms limit her function more than her low-back pain.
aggravating: Walking for more than 5 to 7 minutes

priorManagement.what: Anti-inflammatory medication and simple analgesics with partial benefit
Twelve weeks of supervised physical therapy and exercise
Technically adequate right L5 selective nerve-root block with substantial but temporary relief of leg pain
Activity modification without restoration of walking tolerance

history.preference: She prefers a durable improvement but is concerned about an extensive operation and wants to understand reasonable alternatives.

examination.finding: Independent, with mild difficulty during right heel walking
Mild intermittent hypoesthesia over the dorsum of the right foot

investigations.rationale: Sample: why lumbar_mri is requested now

report.title: Lumbar MRI report

sections.heading: Technique
lines: Supine MRI of the lumbar spine: sagittal T1 and T2; axial T2 at L3-L4, L4-L5, and L5-S1.

sections.heading: Findings
lines: L4-L5: grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis. Translation measures approximately 2.5 mm on this supine study.
L4-L5: a broad disc bulge, advanced facet hypertrophy, and ligamentum flavum thickening produce severe central and bilateral lateral-recess stenosis, right greater than left.
L4-L5: dural sac cross-sectional area approximately 58 mm².
L4-L5 facet joint effusions: right approximately 2.5 mm, left approximately 1.8 mm.
No synovial cyst. No dominant foraminal stenosis.
L3-L4: mild degeneration without clinically significant stenosis.
L5-S1: mild degeneration without clinically relevant stenosis.
No tumor, infection, or fracture.

sections.heading: Impression
lines: Severe multifactorial L4-L5 central and bilateral lateral-recess stenosis, right greater than left, with grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis (approximately 2.5 mm on supine imaging).
Mild, non-dominant degeneration at L3-L4 and L5-S1.

sections.heading: Technique
lines: Lumbar MRI: sagittal T2, axial T2 at L4-L5, and coronal T2.

sections.heading: Findings
lines: Postoperative changes of decompression at L4-L5.

No compressive hematoma. No abscess pattern. No severe cauda equina compression.

lines: Communicating postoperative pseudomeningocele without severe neural compression, hematoma, or abscess pattern.

procedure: Predefined demonstration procedure: complete L4-L5 decompression with bilateral lateral-recess decompression and limited cranial extension into L3-L4.
No fusion and no instrumentation are performed.

checkpoint.title: Intraoperative checkpoint
lines: During decompression of the right lateral recess, the team recognizes a dural defect of approximately 4 mm.
Cerebrospinal fluid is visible at the defect.

team_action: The simulated team performs a primary suture repair with adjunctive sealant.
A Valsalva test at closure is negative.
